newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down as miners fall on zinc price.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down as miners fall on zinc price.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange closed lower Thursday as the mining stocks were again hurt by unstable zinc prices, brokers said.
Investor concern over Peru's current political confusion also weighed the market down, they added.
But the bolsa -- expected to be dominated by the mining sector again Friday -- would likely pick up overall, as investors looked to buy cheap stocks, brokers said.
Thursday, the General Index dropped 2.11 percent to 2,096.9 points as the blue-chip selective index fell 2.06 percent to 3000.0 points, preliminary figures showed.
In a total of 1,662 operations, volume was 32.95 million soles ($14.4 million).
Despite the falls in mining stocks, medium-term prospects for most firms in the sector was bright, brokers said.
"Although zinc prices are falling, we expect fabulous balance sheets in September," said Luis Cueva of Argos brokerage.

Brokers also said foreign and local players showed different attitudes to the country's political crisis, which has seen President Alberto Fujimori plummet in the polls after a recent slew of scandals involving Peru's security forces.
Polymetal miner, Morococha fell 7.97 percent to 6.81 soles on volume of 43,000 shares. Another polymetal miner, Atacocha also fell 4.68 percent to 2.65 soles with a volume of 282,000 shares traded.
The biggest loser among leaders was D'Onofrio, which dropped 10.0 percent to 1.08 soles on volume of 111,000 shares.
The country's leading chocolate and ice cream maker on Thursday reported net profit for the first half of the year of 51,200 soles, compared with 3.7 million soles in the same period last year.

Telefonica del Peru was the biggest winner among leaders, with a 2.52 percent rise to 6.51 soles on a volume of 1.2 million shares. The benchmark bucked the day's trend as investors expected the telecom to report later Thursday good first half results, brokers said.
